id="sdmH2Lh8s6HiHu3jjXA6-22" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">1. Stack Memory</h1><div><ol><li>Stack Memory is the place where all primitive variables, methods and object references are stored.&nbsp;</li><li>Whenever a project executions starts, JVM pushes the method, variables and created object reference in heap memory will be store one by one to the stack.</li><li>Methods will be pushed first in the stack and it defines scope within the stack memory where method level variables and references will be stored.</li><li>Each method scope is isolated with other method scopes. Meaning variables, object references etc won't know about variables and object references stored in another method scope.</li><li>Each Thread will have it's own stack memory but share common heap memory and metaspace.</li><li>When method executions finishes, then method scope will be destroyed in LIFO order.</li><li>When Stack memory became full, JVM will throw StackOverFlowError.</li></ol></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="230" width="640" x="80" y="1240" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="sdmH2Lh8s6HiHu3jjXA6-23" parent="1" 0px;">2. Heap Memory</h1><p></p><ul><li>Heap Memory is the core of JVM where all objects are stored.</li><li>Whenever an object is created using new keyword, a memory will be allocated to the object and it's memory address will be stored into the stack.</li><li>For String literals there will be a special memory allocated called as string pool.</li><li>Inside heap memory, there will be two special memory sections called as</li><ul><li>String Pool, which will have global sope the entire jvm</li><li>Static Pool, which will have per class Scope</li></ul><li><span><b>String Constant Pool</b> is global because <b>content deduplication</b> is safe and universally beneficial across all code</span><span><sup class="superscript"></sup></span><span>. Also String immutable in nature which makes thread to use exact same reference.</span></li><li><span><span><b>Static / Constant Pool</b> is per-class because <b>code execution, symbolic references, and state</b> require strict boundaries and isolation</span><span><sup class="superscript"></sup></span><span>.</span></span></li></ul><p></p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="220" width="810" x="20" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="In Heap memory,&nbsp;<div><ul><li>String literals, String var1 = "test", and String with new keywords, String var2 = new String("test"), are stored differently&nbsp;</li><li>String var1 = "test" is stored in string pool but&nbsp; String var2 = new String("test") will stores outside of string pool.</li><li><b>Reason</b>&nbsp;</li><ul><li>Since JVM stores these two in different manner.</li><li>When two variables have same value i.e. String var1 = "test" and String var2 = "test" then it checks first in the string pool whether object is already there or not. If founds then it will return the same value. Hence, when we do&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;var1 == var2 operation it will return true.</li><li>But when String var1 = new String("test")&nbsp;&amp; String var2 = new String("test")&nbsp; is invoked, then new keyword explicitly commands JVM to allocated new location to each in regular heap memory. Because of the when we do var1 == var2 comparison then it will return false as two memory addresses will be compared.</li></ul></ul></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="250" width="700" x="120" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="sdmH2Lh8s6HiHu3jjXA6-362" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">3. MetaSpace</h1><div><ul><li>This special type of memory which is not part of heap memory neither JVM.</li><li>This part of Native OS memory.</li><li>This will be used to store&nbsp;</li><ul><li>Class structure, templates&nbsp;</li><li>Class metadata which will be referenced from heap memory</li><li>Method bytecode.</li><li>Annotations and class file attributes&nbsp;</li><li>Runtime constant pool i.e. symbolic references, method/field descriptions.</li></ul><li>Before java8, it was part of heap memory and was called as PemGen, which was having fixed memory, which once full throw error i.e. <b>OutOfMemoryError&nbsp;</b>&nbsp;as when multiple classes loads</li><li>With Introduction of metaspace, memory became expandable and pure read-mostly class metadata</li></ul><div><br></div></div><div><b>Internal Architecture &amp; Sizing<br></b></div><div><ul><li>MetaSpace is managed via chunk allocators tied to classloaders</li><ul><li>When <b>ClassLoaader </b>loads classes, the JVM allocates chucks of native memory specifically for that loader.</li><li><span><b>Garbage Collection:</b> Metadata in Metaspace is freed <b>only when its defining <code>ClassLoader</code> itself becomes unreachable and is garbage collected</b></span><span><sup class="superscript"></sup></span><span>. Individual classes loaded by standard system loaders are practically never unloaded.</span></li></ul></ul></div><div><h3>Diagnosing Common Metaspace Issues</h3><p>If your application throws,&nbsp;<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace</span></p><p>It usually indicates a <b>ClassLoader leak</b>, caused by:</p><ol start="1"><li><p><b>Dynamic Bytecode Generation:</b> Excessive runtime proxy generation without caching (e.g., unconstrained CGLIB, ByteBuddy, reflection, or dynamic scripting engines like Groovy/Nashorn).</p></li><li><p><b>App Server Redeployments:</b> Failing to unregister static thread locals, JDBC drivers, or background threads during hot redeployments, preventing the previous application ClassLoader from ever being garbage collected.</p></li></ol></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="490" width="1100" x="20" y="5660" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="sdmH2Lh8s6HiHu3jjXA6-364" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Garbage Collection</h1><div><ul><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Garbage Collection (GC) is the JVM's automatic memory management process that identifies and reclaims memory allocated on the Heap&nbsp; that is no longer reachable by application.</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">GC runs of Algo called <b>Mark &amp; sweep.</b></span></li><li>In this algo, When GC runs,&nbsp;</li><ul><li>Mark Process run where it will mark all object which are ready to be removed from the memory</li><li>When Sweeps run, it will do two thing, first it will remove the objects which were marked earlier and second it will move the surviving object further part of heap memory which will be explained in below section.</li></ul></ul></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="160" width="1080" x="40" y="6160" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="sdmH2Lh8s6HiHu3jjXA6-365" parent="1" Generation&nbsp;</li><li>Old Generation&nbsp;</li></ol></ol><ul><li>In Young Generation Space, all newly created object resides with some defined age.</li><li>This is further divided into 3 parts,</li><ul><li>Eden, everytime new object</li><li>2 Survivor Spaces</li><ul><li>S0</li><li>S1</li></ul></ul><li>In Old generation, Object will stays till it is not reachable to the application. style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=0;" value="GC Supports two algo<div><ol><li>Mark &amp; sweep</li><li>Mark &amp; Sweep with compact memory, here memory fragmentation will be adjust.&nbsp;</li></ol></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="970" x="84" y="8010" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="sdmH2Lh8s6HiHu3jjXA6-449" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;overflow=hidden;rounded=0;" value="<h1 style="margin-top: 0px;">Versions of GC</h1><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">1. Serial GC</span><br><ul><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 14px;">In Serial GC, a single GC thread will run to free up the space.</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 14px;">During execution of Serial GC, whole application threads are paused periodically which is very expensive.</span></li><li><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 14px;">It is very slow</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp;</span></li></ul><div><br></div></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">2. Parallel GC</font></div><div><ul><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">This is default GC in Java 8</font></li><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">This runs in parallel based on CPU core.</font></li><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">This is faster then Serial GC</font></li></ul><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">3. Concurrent GC</font></div></div><div><ul><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">Under this app thread and GC threads run parallely.</font></li><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">But do not to memory compactation.&nbsp;</font></li><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">This will not give 100% grantee that it won't stop app threads.</font></li><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">It was introduction from Java17</font></li></ul><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">4. G1 GC</font></div></div><div><ul><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">This will gives 100% grantee that it won't stop app threads.</font></li><li><font style="font-size: 14px;">Also perform memory compactation.</font></li></ul></div><div><span style="white-space: pre;">	</span><br></div><div><br></div><div><br></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">How to Identify GC Problems?</font></div><div><ul><li><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b>CPU Spikes with Throughput Drop: </b>Application threads freeze while GC threads max out CPU cores running full GC or concurrent marking phases.</font></li><li><p><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b style="">Sawtooth Pattern with an Upward Baseline:</b> Heap usage climbs up, drops during GC, but each drop leaves a higher minimum heap baseline (classic sign of a memory leak).</font></p></li><li><p><font style="font-size: 14px;"><b>High Latency / P99 Spikes:</b> Periodic latency spikes matching GC pause cycles (Stop-The-World events).</font></p></li><li><p><b><font style="font-size: 14px;">OutOfMemoryError (<code>OOM</code>):</font></b></p></li><ul><li><p><font style="font-size: 14px;"><code>java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space</code> (Heap exhaustion or memory leak).</font></p></li><li><p><font style="font-size: 14px;"><code>java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace</code> (ClassLoader leak or excessive dynamic proxies).</font></p></li><li><p><font style="font-size: 14px;"><code style="">java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded</code> (JVM spends over 98% of its time doing GC and recovers less than 2% of the heap).</font></p></li></ul></ul><div><span style="font-size: 14px;"><br></span></div></div><div>Collect Diagnostic Data<span style="font-size: 14px;"></span></div><div><br></div><div><h4>A. Enable Unified GC Logging (Java 9+)</h4><p>GC logs provide the raw timeline of every collection phase, pause duration, and memory shift. Run your application with:</p><div class="code-block ng-tns-c951812425-180 ng-animate-disabled ng-trigger ng-trigger-codeBlockRevealAnimation"><div class="formatted-code-block-internal-container ng-tns-c951812425-180"><div class="animated-opacity ng-tns-c951812425-180"><pre class="ng-tns-c951812425-180"><code role="text" class="code-container formatted ng-tns-c951812425-180">-Xlog:gc*,gc+phases=debug:file=/var/<span class="hljs-built_in">log</span>/jvm/gc.log:time,uptime,pid:filecount=5,filesize=100M<br></code></pre></div></div></div><h4>B. Capture Heap Dumps on Crash</h4><p>Ensure heap dumps are captured automatically when memory runs out:</p><div class="code-block ng-tns-c951812425-181 ng-animate-disabled ng-trigger ng-trigger-codeBlockRevealAnimation"><div class="formatted-code-block-internal-container ng-tns-c951812425-181"><div class="animated-opacity ng-tns-c951812425-181"><pre class="ng-tns-c951812425-181"><code role="text" class="code-container formatted ng-tns-c951812425-181">-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError \<br>-XX:HeapDumpPath=/var/<span class="hljs-built_in">log</span>/jvm/heapdump.hprof<br></code></pre></div></div></div><h4>C. On-Demand Diagnostics (JDK CLI Tools)</h4><p>For a running process (<code>&lt;PID&gt;</code>):</p><ul><li><p><b>Live GC Stats:</b></p><div class="code-block ng-tns-c951812425-182 ng-animate-disabled ng-trigger ng-trigger-codeBlockRevealAnimation"><div class="formatted-code-block-internal-container ng-tns-c951812425-182"><div class="animated-opacity ng-tns-c951812425-182"><pre class="ng-tns-c951812425-182"><code role="text" class="code-container formatted ng-tns-c951812425-182">jstat -gcutil &lt;PID&gt; 1000 <span class="hljs-comment"># Prints Eden, Survivor, Old, Metaspace % usage and GC pause counts <br>every 1s</span><br></code></pre></div></div></div></li><li><p><b>Trigger Heap Dump Manually:</b></p><div class="code-block ng-tns-c951812425-183 ng-animate-disabled ng-trigger ng-trigger-codeBlockRevealAnimation"><div class="formatted-code-block-internal-container ng-tns-c951812425-183"><div class="animated-opacity ng-tns-c951812425-183"><pre class="ng-tns-c951812425-183"><code role="text" class="code-container formatted ng-tns-c951812425-183">jcmd &lt;PID&gt; GC.heap_dump /tmp/dump.hprof<br></code></pre></div></div></div></li><li><p><b>Check Class Histogram (Lightweight Object Count):</b></p><div class="code-block ng-tns-c951812425-184 ng-animate-disabled ng-trigger ng-trigger-codeBlockRevealAnimation"><div class="formatted-code-block-internal-container ng-tns-c951812425-184"><div class="animated-opacity ng-tns-c951812425-184"><pre class="ng-tns-c951812425-184"><code role="text" class="code-container formatted ng-tns-c951812425-184">jcmd &lt;PID&gt; GC.class_histogram<br><br><h3 style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"> Analyse: Tools &amp; Techniques</h3><h4 style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">A. Analysing GC Logs</h4><p style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Upload your <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">gc.log</code> to an analyser like <b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">GCViewer</b> (open source) or <b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">GCEasy</b>:</p><p style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Look for these critical metrics:</p><ol start="1" style="padding-inline-start: 32px; font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><p style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">GC Throughput:</b> Percentage of time the JVM spends executing application code vs running GC. Healthy production services should maintain <b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">&gt; 95% throughput</b> (ideally &gt; 99%).</p></li><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><p style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Max / Average Pause Times:</b> Compare your target pause time (e.g., <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200</code>) against the actual pause times.</p></li><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><p style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Full GC Frequency:</b> Full GCs should be rare or zero during normal operation. Frequent Full GCs indicate Old Gen or Metaspace exhaustion.</p></li><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><p style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Premature Promotion:</b> If short-lived objects are promoted into the Old Generation too quickly (often caused by small Survivor or Eden spaces), the Old Gen fills rapidly, triggering frequent Major/Full GCs.</p></li></ol><h4 style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">B. Analysing Heap Dumps (<code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">.hprof</code>)</h4><p style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Open the <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">.hprof</code> file in <b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Eclipse Memory Analyzer Tool (MAT)</b> or <b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">IntelliJ IDEA Profiler</b>:</p><ol start="1" style="padding-inline-start: 32px; font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><p style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Run the "Leak Suspects Report":</b> Identifies large single object graphs retaining substantial heap percentages.</p></li><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><p style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Dominator Tree:</b> Sort objects by <b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Retained Heap</b> (memory that would be freed if that specific object were garbage collected), not just <b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Shallow Heap</b> (size of the single object itself).</p></li><li style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><p style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Path to GC Roots:</b> For the suspicious object, inspect the incoming references excluding soft/weak references (<code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Path to GC Roots -&gt; exclude all phantom/weak/soft references</code>). This pinpoints exactly which static variable, active thread, or cache is keeping the instance alive.</p></li></ol><h3 style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">4. Common Root Causes and Fixes</h3><table style="margin-bottom: 32px; font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><thead style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><tr style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><strong style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin: 0px !important;">Observation</strong></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><strong style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin: 0px !important;">Root Cause</strong></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><strong style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin: 0px !important;">Remediation</strong></td></tr></thead><tbody style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><tr style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">High Retained Heap in HashMaps/Lists</b></span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Memory leak via unevicted caches or static collections.</span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Use bounded, time-evicting caches (e.g., Caffeine) or Weak/Soft references instead of raw static collections.</span></td></tr><tr style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Frequent Young GC / High Allocation Rate</b></span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Creating excessive short-lived objects (e.g., inside loops, heavy string concatenation).</span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Optimize data structures, reuse buffers, use <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">StringBuilder</code>, or apply object pooling where appropriate.</span></td></tr><tr style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Premature Promotion to Old Gen</b></span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Eden or Survivor spaces are too small for peak object lifespan.</span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Increase young gen size (<code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">-XX:NewRatio</code> or <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">-Xmn</code>) or adjust <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">-XX:SurvivorRatio</code> and <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">-XX:MaxTenuringThreshold</code>.</span></td></tr><tr style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Metaspace OOM / Frequent Full GC</b></span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Dynamic proxy generation (CGLIB/ByteBuddy/reflection) creating unique uncollectable classes.</span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Cap and tune <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">-XX:MaxMetaspaceSize</code>, check for unclosed ClassLoaders or dynamic script compilation leaks.</span></td></tr><tr style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Long Stop-The-World Pauses with G1</b></span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Heap fragmentation or oversized regions during high throughput.</span></td><td style="border: 1px solid rgb(196, 199, 197); padding: 8px 12px; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;"><span style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">Tune <code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis</code>, increase heap size, or transition to <b style="line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">ZGC</b> (<code style="font-family: &quot;Google Sans Text&quot;, sans-serif !important; line-height: 1.15 !important; margin-top: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px !important; margin-right: 0px !important;">-XX:+UseZGC</code>) for sub-millisecond pause requirements.</span></td></tr></tbody></table></code></pre></div></div></div></li></ul><h3></h3></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="2040" width="1606" x="84" y="8110" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

ol.li: Stack Memory is the place where all primitive variables, methods and object references are stored.
Whenever a project executions starts, JVM pushes the method, variables and created object reference in heap memory will be store one by one to the stack.
Methods will be pushed first in the stack and it defines scope within the stack memory where method level variables and references will be stored.
Each method scope is isolated with other method scopes. Meaning variables, object references etc won't know about variables and object references stored in another method scope.
Each Thread will have it's own stack memory but share common heap memory and metaspace.
When method executions finishes, then method scope will be destroyed in LIFO order.
When Stack memory became full, JVM will throw StackOverFlowError.

ul.li: Heap Memory is the core of JVM where all objects are stored.
Whenever an object is created using new keyword, a memory will be allocated to the object and it's memory address will be stored into the stack.
For String literals there will be a special memory allocated called as string pool.
Inside heap memory, there will be two special memory sections called as
String Pool, which will have global sope the entire jvm
Static Pool, which will have per class Scope

li.span: String Constant Pool is global because content deduplication is safe and universally beneficial across all code
. Also String immutable in nature which makes thread to use exact same reference.

span.span: Static / Constant Pool is per-class because code execution, symbolic references, and state require strict boundaries and isolation

div.div:
In Heap memory,
String literals, String var1 = "test", and String with new keywords, String var2 = new String("test"), are stored differently
String var1 = "test" is stored in string pool but String var2 = new String("test") will stores outside of string pool.
Reason
Since JVM stores these two in different manner.
When two variables have same value i.e. String var1 = "test" and String var2 = "test" then it checks first in the string pool whether object is already there or not. If founds then it will return the same value. Hence, when we do var1 == var2 operation it will return true.
But when String var1 = new String("test") & String var2 = new String("test") is invoked, then new keyword explicitly commands JVM to allocated new location to each in regular heap memory. Because of the when we do var1 == var2 comparison then it will return false as two memory addresses will be compared.

ul.li: This special type of memory which is not part of heap memory neither JVM.
This part of Native OS memory.
This will be used to store
Class structure, templates
Class metadata which will be referenced from heap memory
Method bytecode.
Annotations and class file attributes
Runtime constant pool i.e. symbolic references, method/field descriptions.
Before java8, it was part of heap memory and was called as PemGen, which was having fixed memory, which once full throw error i.e. OutOfMemoryError as when multiple classes loads
With Introduction of metaspace, memory became expandable and pure read-mostly class metadata
MetaSpace is managed via chunk allocators tied to classloaders
When ClassLoaader loads classes, the JVM allocates chucks of native memory specifically for that loader.

li.span: Garbage Collection: Metadata in Metaspace is freed only when its defining ClassLoader itself becomes unreachable and is garbage collected
. Individual classes loaded by standard system loaders are practically never unloaded.

div.p: If your application throws, java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace
It usually indicates a ClassLoader leak, caused by:

li.p: Dynamic Bytecode Generation: Excessive runtime proxy generation without caching (e.g., unconstrained CGLIB, ByteBuddy, reflection, or dynamic scripting engines like Groovy/Nashorn).

App Server Redeployments: Failing to unregister static thread locals, JDBC drivers, or background threads during hot redeployments, preventing the previous application ClassLoader from ever being garbage collected.

li.span: Garbage Collection (GC) is the JVM's automatic memory management process that identifies and reclaims memory allocated on the Heap that is no longer reachable by application.
GC runs of Algo called Mark & sweep.

ul.li: In this algo, When GC runs,
Mark Process run where it will mark all object which are ready to be removed from the memory

When Sweeps run, it will do two thing, first it will remove the objects which were marked earlier and second it will move the surviving object further part of heap memory which will be explained in below section.

ul.li: Heap Memory is divided into 2 spaces
In Young Generation Space, all newly created object resides with some defined age.
This is further divided into 3 parts,
Eden, everytime new object
2 Survivor Spaces
S0
S1
In Old generation, Object will stays till it is not reachable to the application. Meaning no age is defined.

li.span: In Serial GC, a single GC thread will run to free up the space.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 14px;

li.span: During execution of Serial GC, whole application threads are paused periodically which is very expensive.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 14px;

li.span: It is very slow
This is default GC in Java 8
This runs in parallel based on CPU core.
This is faster then Serial GC
Under this app thread and GC threads run parallely.
But do not to memory compactation.
This will not give 100% grantee that it won't stop app threads.
It was introduction from Java17
This will gives 100% grantee that it won't stop app threads.
Also perform memory compactation.
CPU Spikes with Throughput Drop: Application threads freeze while GC threads max out CPU cores running full GC or concurrent marking phases.

p.span: Sawtooth Pattern with an Upward Baseline: Heap usage climbs up, drops during GC, but each drop leaves a higher minimum heap baseline (classic sign of a memory leak).
High Latency / P99 Spikes: Periodic latency spikes matching GC pause cycles (Stop-The-World events).
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space (Heap exhaustion or memory leak).
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace (ClassLoader leak or excessive dynamic proxies).
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded (JVM spends over 98% of its time doing GC and recovers less than 2% of the heap).

div.p: GC logs provide the raw timeline of every collection phase, pause duration, and memory shift. Run your application with:
div.h4: B. Capture Heap Dumps on Crash
div.p: Ensure heap dumps are captured automatically when memory runs out:

pre.code:
jstat -gcutil <PID> 1000 # Prints Eden, Survivor, Old, Metaspace % usage and GC pause counts
every 1s

jcmd <PID> GC.class_histogram
Analyse: Tools & Techniques
A. Analysing GC Logs
Upload your gc.log to an analyser like GCViewer (open source) or GCEasy:
Look for these critical metrics:
GC Throughput: Percentage of time the JVM spends executing application code vs running GC. Healthy production services should maintain > 95% throughput (ideally > 99%).
Max / Average Pause Times: Compare your target pause time (e.g., -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200) against the actual pause times.
Full GC Frequency: Full GCs should be rare or zero during normal operation. Frequent Full GCs indicate Old Gen or Metaspace exhaustion.
Premature Promotion: If short-lived objects are promoted into the Old Generation too quickly (often caused by small Survivor or Eden spaces), the Old Gen fills rapidly, triggering frequent Major/Full GCs.
B. Analysing Heap Dumps (.hprof)
Open the .hprof file in Eclipse Memory Analyzer Tool (MAT) or IntelliJ IDEA Profiler:
Run the "Leak Suspects Report": Identifies large single object graphs retaining substantial heap percentages.
Dominator Tree: Sort objects by Retained Heap (memory that would be freed if that specific object were garbage collected), not just Shallow Heap (size of the single object itself).
Path to GC Roots: For the suspicious object, inspect the incoming references excluding soft/weak references (Path to GC Roots -> exclude all phantom/weak/soft references). This pinpoints exactly which static variable, active thread, or cache is keeping the instance alive.
4. Common Root Causes and Fixes
ObservationRoot CauseRemediation
High Retained Heap in HashMaps/ListsMemory leak via unevicted caches or static collections.Use bounded, time-evicting caches (e.g., Caffeine) or Weak/Soft references instead of raw static collections.
Frequent Young GC / High Allocation RateCreating excessive short-lived objects (e.g., inside loops, heavy string concatenation).Optimize data structures, reuse buffers, use StringBuilder, or apply object pooling where appropriate.
Premature Promotion to Old GenEden or Survivor spaces are too small for peak object lifespan.Increase young gen size (-XX:NewRatio or -Xmn) or adjust -XX:SurvivorRatio and -XX:MaxTenuringThreshold.
Metaspace OOM / Frequent Full GCDynamic proxy generation (CGLIB/ByteBuddy/reflection) creating unique uncollectable classes.Cap and tune -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize, check for unclosed ClassLoaders or dynamic script compilation leaks.
Long Stop-The-World Pauses with G1Heap fragmentation or oversized regions during high throughput.Tune -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis, increase heap size, or transition to ZGC (-XX:+UseZGC) for sub-millisecond pause requirements.
